children: , the hybrid-cloud and quantum-computing company, fell approximately 3.1% to $240.77 Wednesday after securing a finalized $1 billion Commerce Department award for subsidiary Anderon. The funding gives IBM a major boost for its quantum-manufacturing ambitions without forcing the company to shoulder the entire investment itself. The valuation snapshot also shows IBM trading just 0.79% below its $242.69 GF Value, suggesting the shares remain close to GuruFocus' estimate of fair value despite Wednesday's drop.

Anderon operates a 300-millimeter quantum-wafer foundry in Albany, New York, where the first wafers are already moving through production. IBM is committing another $1 billion alongside the government award, taking the program to $2 billion before including earlier investment in the site. The facility is designed to manufacture superconducting qubit arrays, quantum input-output signaling systems and readout-chain components, with additional architectures expected to follow as the platform expands.

The financing structure is the most interesting part for investors. Federal funding effectively matches IBM's disclosed cash commitment dollar for dollar, giving the company significantly more manufacturing capacity for every dollar it puts directly into the project. Anderon could eventually become infrastructure not only for IBM but also for outside quantum-chip designers. That opportunity remains unproven, however: IBM has yet to disclose customers, contracted wafer volumes, pricing or expected foundry revenue. For now, the project strengthens IBM's quantum infrastructure story, but the next meaningful test will be whether technological capacity turns into commercial demand.

title: IBM Falls Over 3% After Quantum Foundry Secures $1 Billion
